blocks.source: Vol IV, Adversarial Verification, § Fault Injection on Hardware
blocks.md: A fault injected in simulation tests only the modeled response. On physical machinery, bus contention, microcontroller clock drift, DMA stalls, and transient voltage drops across inductive motor drivers determine whether a safety intervention executes before physical impact. When a simulator fails to capture and calibrate these physical interactions, simulation alone cannot substantiate claims that depend on them.

options: Faults come from inverting each recorded design guarantee at its handoff and from working forward from the physical machine, each built as a five-element chain from cause to violated claim.
Extreme value theory fits the distribution of block maxima or threshold exceedances, so a tail estimate needs many independent extremes and a justified tail family.

A transduction attack delivers a checksum-valid packet whose measurement is false, so packet integrity is never an oracle for perception, and a wrong action inside the envelope after prompt injection or a patch is a coverage deficit, never a pass.

Each fault record binds a signed header (trial, claim, envelope point, injection, oracle digest, latencies, margins, verdict) to the independently retained trace, carrying evidence and its gaps to release.
